title: What is SQL Server?
description: Learn what SQL Server is, its architecture, editions, and the tools and services it provides.

data.text: What is SQL Server?
SQL Server is a relational database management system (RDBMS) developed and marketed by Microsoft.

Similar to other RDBMS software, SQL Server is built on top of SQL, a standard programming language for interacting with relational databases. SQL Server is tied to Transact-SQL, or T-SQL, Microsoft's implementation of SQL, which includes a set of proprietary programming constructs.

SQL Server ran only on Windows for more than 20 years. That changed with SQL Server 2017 (released in October 2017), the first release that ran on both Windows and Linux. Today SQL Server also runs in containers and as a managed service in Azure (Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance).
SQL Server Architecture
SQL Server consists of two main components: the Database Engine and SQLOS (SQL Server Operating System).

data.alt: What is SQL Server - SQL Server Architecture

items: Database Engine – the core component that processes queries and manages database files, pages, and indexes.
SQLOS – provides operating system services such as memory and I/O management, exception handling, and synchronization.

data.text: Database Engine
The core component of SQL Server is the Database Engine, which comprises a relational engine that processes queries and a storage engine that manages database files, pages, and indexes.
Additionally, the database engine creates database objects such as stored procedures, views, and triggers.
Relational Engine

The Relational Engine contains the components that determine the optimal method for executing a query. It is also known as the query processor. The relational engine requests data from the storage engine based on the input query and processes the results.
Some tasks of the relational engine include query processing, memory management, thread and task management, buffer management, and distributed query processing.
Storage Engine
The storage engine is responsible for storing and retrieving data from storage systems such as disks and SAN.
SQLOS

Under the relational engine and storage engine lies the SQL Server Operating System, or SQLOS. SQLOS provides various operating system services such as memory and I/O management, as well as exception handling and synchronization services.
SQL Server Services and Tools
Microsoft offers both data management and business intelligence (BI) tools and services alongside SQL Server.

data.title: Development & Management
items: SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) for database development
SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) for managing, deploying, and monitoring databases

data.title: Data Analysis & Reporting
items: SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS) for data analysis
SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) for reports and data visualization
Machine Learning Services (originally R Services, introduced in SQL Server 2016)

data.text: SQL Server Editions

SQL Server has five primary editions. Two are free of charge (Developer and Express) and three are licensed (Standard, Enterprise, and Web). Enterprise is a superset of Standard, so feature differences matter when you read about partitioning, compression, or Always On availability groups.

cards.title: Developer Edition
cards.description: Intended for database development and testing purposes. Free of charge.

cards.title: Express Edition
cards.description: Suitable for small databases with a storage capacity of up to 10 GB per database. Free of charge.

cards.title: Enterprise Edition
cards.description: Includes all SQL Server features. For larger and more critical applications.

cards.title: Standard Edition
cards.description: A subset of Enterprise Edition features with limitations on processor cores and memory.

cards.title: Web Edition
cards.description: A good option for web hosting companies due to low total cost of ownership.

data.text: Check the Version and Edition You Are Running
Before you blame the database for a missing feature, confirm which version and edition you are connected to. Both are available from T-SQL:

data.title: Inspect the server version, edition, and current database
data.content: Run this in SSMS or Azure Data Studio against any database. The major version number tells you which feature set you have: 16.x is SQL Server 2022, 15.x is 2019, 14.x is 2017, and 13.x is 2016.
data.code:
SELECT
    @@VERSION AS version_string,
    SERVERPROPERTY('ProductMajorVersion') AS major_version,
    SERVERPROPERTY('Edition') AS edition,
    SERVERPROPERTY('EngineEdition') AS engine_edition,
    DB_NAME() AS current_database;

data.title: Interview answer
data.text: Describe SQL Server as Microsoft's relational engine plus SQLOS, where the relational engine parses, optimizes, and executes a query and the storage engine reads and writes 8 KB pages through the buffer pool. Mentioning the buffer pool and the plan cache shows you understand the architecture, not just the syntax.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SQL Server is a relational database management system developed by Microsoft.
Its architecture includes the Database Engine (Relational + Storage engines) and SQLOS.
SQL Server offers various editions: Developer, Express, Enterprise, Standard, and Web.
Tools like SSMS, SSIS, SSAS, and SSRS support the full data lifecycle.
